'''Jürgen Meyer-ter-Vehn''' (born 16 February 1940 in [[Berlin|Berlin, Germany]]) is a German [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who specializes in laser-plasma interactions at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics|Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.mpq.mpg.de/lpg/grouphp/JMeyerterVehn/personalPage.html|title=Jürgen Meyer-ter-Vehn|website=www2.mpq.mpg.de|access-date=2020-03-12}}</ref> He published under the name '''Meyer''' until 1973.

Meyer-ter-Vehn's work involved examining the physical principles of [[inertial fusion]] with lasers and heavy [[ion beam]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Henig|first1=A.|last2=Steinke|first2=S.|last3=Schnürer|first3=M.|last4=Sokollik|first4=T.|last5=Hörlein|first5=R.|last6=Kiefer|first6=D.|last7=Jung|first7=D.|last8=Schreiber|first8=J.|last9=Hegelich|first9=B. == Life ==
From 1959, Meyer-ter-Vehn studied physics at the [[University of Münster]] and [[LMU Munich]] as a scholarship holder of the [[German National Academic Foundation]], where he obtained his diploma in 1966. In 1969, he received his doctorate in theoretical [[nuclear physics]] from the [[Technical University of Munich]]. He researched at the Technical University of Munich, the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]] and the [[Jülich Research Center]]. In 1976, he habilitated at the Technical University of Munich, where he has been an associate professor since 1997. From 1979, he was in the laser research group of the [[Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics]] in Munich, from which the Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics emerged in 1981. Until 2005, he was group leader for laser plasma theory.

Until the end of the 1970s, he mainly dealt with theoretical nuclear physics.

He was married to Helga Meyer-ter-Vehn (died 2011) and has two sons, Tobias Meyer-ter-Vehn and Moritz Meyer-ter-Vehn, and four granddaughters, Rebekka, Lili, Clara, and Sophie.

== Honors and awards ==
In 1997, Meyer-ter-Vehn received the [[American Nuclear Society]]'s [[Edward Teller Award]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Edward Teller lectures: lasers and inertial fusion energy|date=2005|publisher=Imperial College|others=Hora, Heinrich, 1931-, Miley, George H. (George Hunter), 1933-|isbn=1-86094-727-1|location=London|oclc=232159974}}</ref> In 2009, he received the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] from the [[European Physical Society]] for ''"his seminal theoretical work in the fields of [[inertial confinement fusion]] (ICF), relativistic laser–plasma interaction and [[Laser-wakefield acceleration|laser wakefield electron acceleration]]".''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jacquemot|first=Sylvie|date=2009|title=36th European Physical Society Conference on Plasma Physics|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|language=en|volume=51|issue=12|article-number=120201|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/51/12/120201|issn=0741-3335|doi-access=free}}</ref>
